held_out_rule: A case is held_out iff the first byte of SHA-256(UTF-8('frf-ms-eval-v1' + NUL + case_id)) is >= 0x80; otherwise it is development. The rule is fixed before measurement. It is a selection-leakage control, not a temporal holdout.
resource_metrics: wall_time_ms: parent-measured monotonic elapsed time around the isolated child
peak_rss_kb: Maximum resident set size reported by /usr/bin/time -v (ru_maxrss on Linux), falling back to /proc/self/status VmHWM
output_bytes: exact byte length of the child's canonical observation
receipt_rule: A receipt is emitted only when wall_time_ms, peak_rss_kb (>0), output_bytes, input_sha256, observed_sha256, toolchain, image, and exact command are present. Every reported advantage must name at least one receipt whose observed field equals the claimed observation.
blocked_controls: D6-detector-live-miri: live detector execution is NOT_RUN in the default image; it is never counted as a pass.
R5-proof-live-coq: live Coq checking is NOT_RUN in the default image; manifest parsing is not proof acceptance.
E6-discovery-authentic-chain: an authentic native FRF/FRF-Fuzz/Gemel chain is NOT_RUN without FRF_BRIDGE_LIVE_BUNDLE; modeled/substitute evidence is not a substitute.

hypotheses.name: founded-graph-support
hypotheses.claim: Least-fixed-point support rejects ungrounded cycles, all-node certificates expose hidden intermediate and shared-mapping dependencies, and exact cuts preserve unrelated support, whereas greatest-fixed-point, root-only-certificate, direct-premise, and over-cut baselines do not.
hypotheses.decision_rule: Every production support arm matches its preregistered expected observation on every held-out support case. Each named naive support arm fails at least one preregistered discriminator on a held-out case.

hypotheses.name: path-alias-semantics
hypotheses.claim: Exact, descendant, shared-mapping, and top aliases produce distinct qualified outcomes, and omission is distinguished from not-falsified; boolean aliasing and absence-collapsing baselines lose at least one of those distinctions.
hypotheses.decision_rule: Every production path arm matches its preregistered expected observation on every held-out path case. Each named naive path arm diverges from production on at least one preregistered held-out discriminator.

hypotheses.name: calibrated-detector
hypotheses.claim: Calibrated detector evidence accepts authentic known-bad/known-good receipts and refuses raw-stdout acceptance without a typed finding, dead detectors, misconfigured builds, and mock-provider transport; job-success, raw-stdout, and origin-ignoring baselines accept at least one such invalid receipt.
hypotheses.decision_rule: The production detector arm refuses every preregistered adversarial receipt on held-out cases. At least one named naive detector baseline accepts a held-out adversarial receipt. Live detector execution is reported as typed NOT_RUN, never as a pass.

hypotheses.name: proof-closure-correspondence
hypotheses.claim: Closure plus the separate implementation-correspondence gate rejects an unchecked FFI wrapper and a missing reentrant transition, while a parser-only baseline accepts the same manifests.
hypotheses.decision_rule: The production proof arm rejects every preregistered invalid manifest on held-out cases. The parser-only baseline accepts at least one held-out invalid manifest. No live-checker acceptance is claimed without a live checker run.

hypotheses.name: empirical-discovery
hypotheses.claim: Bridge verification refuses modeled and substitute providers, stale candidates, and tampered external objects; provenance-ignoring and schema-only baselines accept at least one such invalid bundle. An authentic native chain is typed NOT_RUN when unavailable, not synthesized.
hypotheses.decision_rule: The production bridge arm refuses or correctly not-runs every preregistered bundle. At least one named naive discovery baseline accepts a held-out invalid bundle. The authentic-chain control is reported as typed NOT_RUN.

hypotheses.name: decision-quality
hypotheses.claim: On the preregistered known-bad and known-good control families, production arms make no false-accept or false-refuse decisions on held-out cases, while at least one naive baseline makes a false-accept or false-refuse decision somewhere in the corpus.
hypotheses.decision_rule: For cases with truth=reject, a production arm is a false accept iff its observed label is in the case's accept_outcomes. For truth=accept, it is a false refuse iff its observed label is not in accept_outcomes and is not NOT_RUN. NOT_RUN cases are censored and reported separately. Production false_accept and false_refuse must both be zero on held-out cases. At least one named naive baseline must have false_accept + false_refuse > 0 across the corpus (development or held-out). Baselines with zero false decisions are reported as negative findings, not hidden. A baseline with no decision case anywhere is reported as not_evaluated.

cases.description: Grounded cycle: admitted leaf a supports p, p and q support each other.
Self-cycle q <- q with no admitted entry point.
Mutual cycle p <-> q with no admitted entry point.
Excluding intermediate u must cut q; a root-only certificate hides u.
Excluding shared premise m must cut both routes to q; direct-premise reasoning misses the shared dependency.
Excluding u cuts q but must retain unrelated r supported through w <- b.
Excluding u must cut q on the exact-cut arm; the over-cut baseline also cuts q.
An exact whole-object write overlaps a live descendant read; both production and boolean aliasing report a conflict.
Two disjoint descendant ranges must be compatible; boolean aliasing treats them as may-alias.
A shared-mapping view is not an independent exact allocation; a disjoint explicit range still preserves shared-mapping uncertainty, while a mapping-as-independent baseline fabricates compatibility.
A top alias makes the overlap possible, not definite; treating top as exact fabricates a conflict.
A legally absent unobserved callback is omission; a non-absent unobserved callback is not_falsified.
A foreign-unknown provider preserves uncertainty; ignoring it fabricates compatibility.
Writes through aliases of two distinct objects are compatible; both arms agree.
Authentic known-bad detection plus a clean known-good control is calibrated.
A known-bad case prints the diagnostic text but supplies no typed finding.
A known-bad case exits zero with no finding; the detector is dead.
A typed finding exists but the detector build omits the required sanitizer flag.
An otherwise valid receipt is transported by a mock provider.
Live Miri execution is opt-in and absent in the default image.
Approved digest-bound manifest: admission and correspondence pass, but no live checker is configured.
The theorem is admitted but the FFI wrapper is unchecked.
A reachable dependency is Admitted.
The implementation binding omits the mandatory reentrant callback transition.
Live Coq checking is opt-in and absent in the default image.
All external objects are declared modeled with native DSO and matched re-execution.
The provider is declared a substitute.
The bundle expected candidate differs from the observation candidate.
The FRF-Fuzz finding bytes are changed without updating its declared identity.
No external observations are supplied; the bridge must be typed NOT_RUN.
An authentic native chain is available only when FRF_BRIDGE_LIVE_BUNDLE names a verified capture.

claims.text: The shipped least-fixed-point evaluator rejects ungrounded self and mutual cycles.
The greatest-fixed-point baseline accepts those same ungrounded cycles.
All-node certificates expose hidden intermediate and shared-mapping dependencies at the exact cut.
Root-only and direct-premise baselines miss the exact cut.
Exact cuts preserve unrelated support, while over-cut loses it.
Exact footprint semantics distinguishes disjoint descendant ranges and preserves shared-mapping uncertainty, while boolean aliasing and mapping-as-independent baselines do not.
The detector adjudicator refuses raw-stdout, dead, misconfigured, and mock evidence; job-success and raw-stdout baselines accept it.
Closure plus correspondence rejects an unchecked FFI wrapper and a missing reentrant transition, while parser-only acceptance does not.
The bridge refuses modeled and substitute providers, stale candidates, and tampered external objects, while provenance-ignoring and schema-only baselines accept them.

On held-out known-bad and known-good controls, production arms make no false-accept or false-refuse decisions, and at least one named naive baseline makes a false decision somewhere in the corpus; zero-error baselines are reported as negative findings.
Live detector execution, live Coq checking, and an authentic native chain are typed NOT_RUN in the default environment; no pass is fabricated.
